questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Azerbaijan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Azerbaijan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Azerbaijan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.proof: It borders on Russia in the north, Georgia and, Armenia in the west, Iran in the south, and the Caspian Sea on the east.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Azerbaijan?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “History” part of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.proof: Over the centuries, as the original population mingled with the immigrant Turkic nomads, the number of native Persian speakers gradually diminished, and a Turkic dialect nowadays known as Azerbaijani (or Azerbaijani Turkic) gained hold.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Azerbaijan?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Economy” part of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.proof: Azerbaijan's currency is the Azerbaijani manat (AZN) which is divided into 100 qəpik.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “Because Azerbaijan is close to Europe and its history is related to Europe, Azerbaijan is a member of a number of European groups, including the Council of Europe since _____.”

hints.nudge: It is a year in the twenty-first century.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Azerbaijan article.

questions.proof: Because Azerbaijan is close to Europe and its history is related to Europe, Azerbaijan is a member of a number of European groups, including the Council of Europe since 2001.
